basis: Glycosylation disorder; hepatic injury in 5/5 with liver failure in 2/5; developmental impairment in 3/4. Splenomegaly alone does not establish blood-organ damage.
Carcinoma arising in the rectum; glandular and squamous differentiation do not imply additional organs.
Explicitly nonsyndromic early-onset cataract; WFS1 alone does not establish endocrine or neurologic disease.
Inherited anemia umbrella; metabolic, intestinal and hepatic abnormalities vary among subtypes and are not universal features.
Water-induced urticaria is a mast-cell-mediated skin disorder; its precise trigger is uncertain. No additional organ damage is established.
Joubert neurodevelopmental disorder; eye-movement abnormalities and disordered breathing reflect central dysfunction. Coloboma and hearing loss are each under 30%.
Benign neoplasm of vascular tissue; skin localization is not established across the entire umbrella.
Inflammatory liver disease with infectious, autoimmune, toxic and metabolic causes; no single mechanism applies throughout the umbrella.
Autoimmune destruction of red cells and platelets defines the syndrome; bruising, jaundice and dyspnea do not establish additional organ damage.
Defined by obesity and chronic alveolar hypoventilation with hypercapnia; secondary polycythemia does not establish an intrinsic blood disorder.
Hypoxic-ischemic injury targets brain tissue; localized vascular obstruction or systemic hypoperfusion are alternative causes, not required additional organ damage.
Noninflammatory skeletal dysplasia with progressive joint degeneration and contractures; the pseudorheumatoid name does not establish autoimmunity.
Senior-Loken syndrome is defined by nephronophthisis and retinal dystrophy; kidney failure reported in 21/21 and rod-cone dystrophy in 7/21.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay define the disorder; strabismus and frontal hair loss each occur in 30-79%. Facial dysmorphism alone adds no axis.
TRIOBP-related nonsyndromic severe-to-profound sensorineural hearing loss.
Squamous carcinoma of the lacrimal gland, which belongs to the ocular axis.
Ornithine metabolism defect defined by progressive chorioretinal degeneration; aminoaciduria alone is not renal damage. Hearing loss and seizures are under 30%.
Direct amoebic infection of brain tissue; extracerebral dissemination is not established in at least 30%.
Infantile Pompe disease defines storage myopathy and cardiomyopathy; cerebral white-matter lesions reported in 80-99%. Respiratory failure is muscular; hepatomegaly alone adds no liver axis.
Predominantly a peritoneal mesothelial tumor; less common pleural variants do not establish pulmonary disease across most patients.
Nonbacterial erosion of tooth dentine; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Congenital finger-extensor tendon abnormality; multiple lipomas and xanthomatosis are reported in 80-99%, supporting subcutaneous involvement.
Inflammation directly affects myocardial interstitium; granulomas and giant cells alone do not establish a specific infectious or autoimmune cause.
Dementia caused by multiple cerebral infarctions; brain injury defines the disease, while additional cardiovascular organ damage is not required.
Pheochromocytoma and pancreatic islet-cell tumors involve endocrine organs. Episodic hypertension alone does not establish lasting vascular injury; other damage lacks frequency evidence.
